title: Acts Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Acts 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus was taken up into heaven
Jesus commanded the apostles to wait in Jerusalem
Jesus showed himself alive after his passion
The former treatise made to Theophilus
questions.correctAnswer: The former treatise made to Theophilus
questions.explanation: Acts 1:1 introduces the former treatise made to Theophilus before other events.

questions.question: To whom did Jesus give commandments through the Holy Ghost?
options: The apostles whom he had chosen
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles whom he had chosen
questions.explanation: Acts 1:2 states Jesus gave commandments through the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen.

questions.question: How long was Jesus seen alive after his passion?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 mentions Jesus was seen alive by the apostles for forty days after his passion.

questions.question: What did Jesus command the apostles not to do until they received the promise of the Father?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4 records Jesus commanding the apostles not to depart from Jerusalem until they received the promise of the Father.

questions.question: With what did John baptize according to Acts 1?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:5 states John baptized with water.

questions.question: What did Jesus say the apostles would be baptized with soon?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:5 says the apostles would be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.

questions.question: What question did the apostles ask Jesus when they came together?
options: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?
Lord, when will the world end?
Lord, shall we build a temple?
Lord, who is the greatest among us?
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:6 records the apostles asking Jesus if He would restore the kingdom to Israel at that time.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about knowing the times or seasons?
options: It is not for you to know
questions.correctAnswer: It is not for you to know
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 states Jesus told them it is not for them to know the times or seasons which the Father hath put in his own power.

questions.question: What will the apostles receive after the Holy Ghost comes upon them?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8 says the apostles shall receive power after the Holy Ghost comes upon them.

questions.question: Where did Jesus say the apostles would be witnesses?
options: Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8 specifies the apostles will be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

questions.question: What happened to Jesus after he had spoken these things?
options: He was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight
questions.correctAnswer: He was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight
questions.explanation: Acts 1:9 tells that after speaking, Jesus was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight.

questions.question: Jesus showed himself alive to the apostles by many infallible proofs.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 states Jesus showed himself alive by many infallible proofs.

questions.question: The apostles were told to wait in Jerusalem for the promise of the Father.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4 records Jesus commanding the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for the promise of the Father.

questions.question: Jesus said he would restore the kingdom to Israel at that time.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 shows Jesus said it is not for them to know the times or seasons, indicating He did not say He would restore the kingdom at that time.

questions.question: The text says the apostles were baptized with water by Jesus himself.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:5 states John baptized with water, not Jesus.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the two men in white apparel say to the disciples?
options: This same Jesus shall come again
Do not believe in Jesus' resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: This same Jesus shall come again
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Acts 1:11 states, 'this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.'

questions.question: What does Acts 1:5 promise will happen if someone waits for the promise of the Father as commanded in Acts 1:4?
options: They will be baptized with water
questions.explanation: Acts 1:5 states, 'For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.' This indicates that waiting leads to receiving the Holy Spirit, which is the promise of power.

questions.question: How many disciples were gathered in the upper room?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:15 states, 'the number of names together were about an hundred and twenty,' indicating the total number of disciples present.

questions.question: What is stated in Acts 1:16 about Judas?
options: He was not chosen by the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 1:16 refers to Judas as 'guide to them that took Jesus,' indicating his role in the betrayal.

questions.question: What were the disciples doing in Acts 1:14?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:14 explicitly states, 'These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication.'

questions.question: What did Peter assert about Judas in Acts 1:17?
options: He was numbered with the apostles
He was a man of integrity
He was never part of the ministry
questions.correctAnswer: He was numbered with the apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 1:17 states, 'For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry,' confirming that Judas was indeed part of the apostles.

questions.question: How did Judas die according to Acts 1:18?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:18 describes Judas' death: 'falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.'

questions.question: What did the disciples do after witnessing Jesus' ascension, according to Acts 1:12?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:12 states, 'Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet,' indicating their action after witnessing the ascension.

questions.question: Why does Acts 1:7 emphasize the importance of knowing times and seasons?
options: It is not for them to know
It is essential for their ministry
It is a sign of faith
questions.correctAnswer: It is not for them to know
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 states, 'It is not for you to know the times or the seasons,' indicating that certain knowledge is reserved for God alone.

questions.question: What was the focus of Jesus' teachings during the 40 days after his resurrection, as stated in Acts 1:3?
options: Things pertaining to the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: Things pertaining to the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 mentions that Jesus spoke of 'the things pertaining to the kingdom of God' during his post-resurrection appearances.

questions.question: What does Acts 1:8 say believers will receive after the Holy Ghost comes upon them?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8 states, 'But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you,' indicating the empowerment believers will receive.

questions.question: What does Acts 1:4 instruct the apostles to do?
options: Wait for the promise of the Father
questions.correctAnswer: Wait for the promise of the Father
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4 commands the apostles to 'wait for the promise of the Father,' emphasizing patience and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were confused about Jesus' ascension.
questions.explanation: The disciples were gazing into heaven, indicating confusion or wonder about what had just occurred. Acts 1:10 describes their steadfast look towards heaven.

questions.question: True or False: Judas was known for his great faithfulness to Jesus.
questions.explanation: Judas is described as the one who betrayed Jesus, indicating his lack of faithfulness. Acts 1:16 refers to him as 'guide to them that took Jesus.'

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were in disagreement about their next steps after Jesus ascended.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:14 states that they were in 'one accord,' indicating unity in prayer and purpose after Jesus' ascension.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 1.

questions.question: What is the name given in their proper tongue to the field purchased with the reward of iniquity, as mentioned in Acts 1:19?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:19 states that the field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, which means The field of blood.

questions.question: According to Acts 1:20, the scripture from the book of Psalms quoted regarding Judas's place says what about his habitation?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:20 quotes Psalms saying 'Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein.'

questions.question: Who were the two men appointed to be considered to replace Judas, as mentioned in Acts 1:23?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:23 names Joseph called Barsabas, surnamed Justus, and Matthias as the two appointed for consideration.

questions.question: In Acts 1:24, the apostles prayed to the Lord asking Him to show what specific thing?
options: Which of the two He has chosen
When the kingdom will be restored
How to baptize with the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: Which of the two He has chosen
questions.explanation: Acts 1:24 records their prayer asking the Lord to show which one of the two He has chosen.

questions.question: What method was used to select Matthias as the apostle, according to Acts 1:26?
options: They voted by show of hands
The Holy Ghost descended upon him
questions.explanation: Acts 1:26 states that they gave forth their lots and the lot fell upon Matthias.

questions.question: According to Acts 1:22, what is the required qualification for the replacement apostle regarding the period of companionship with Jesus?
options: Companied from John's baptism to Jesus' ascension
Companied during the Last Supper only
questions.correctAnswer: Companied from John's baptism to Jesus' ascension
questions.explanation: Acts 1:22 states the candidate must have accompanied from the baptism of John until Jesus was taken up.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'episkopē' (ἐπισκοπή) in Acts 1:20, translated as 'bishoprick,' mean?
options: Oversight or office of an overseer
questions.correctAnswer: Oversight or office of an overseer
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'episkopē' means oversight or the office of an overseer, fitting the context of apostolic succession in Acts 1:20.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Acts 1:20 when citing Psalms about Judas’s desolation?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:20 uses allusion by referencing Psalm texts to explain Judas's fate.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is directly referenced in Acts 1:20 concerning the desolation of Judas's dwelling?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:20 references Psalm 69:25 which speaks of a desolate habitation, fulfilled in Judas's case.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of apostolic succession and replacement seen in Acts 1:22-26?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 3:1-7 discusses qualifications for overseers, paralleling the qualifications and replacement of apostles in Acts 1:22-26.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the apostles casting lots to choose Judas's replacement in Acts chapter 1?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:24 records the apostles praying before casting lots in Acts 1:26.

questions.question: What typological significance does the field called Aceldama (field of blood) hold in the context of Judas's betrayal and death as narrated in Acts 1?
options: It symbolizes the judgment and consequence of betrayal
It is an image of paradise lost
It represents the place of Jesus’ birth
It foreshadows the gathering of the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the judgment and consequence of betrayal
questions.explanation: Acts 1:18-19 shows the field of blood as a symbol of Judas's betrayal and the resulting judgment, typifying consequence in biblical narrative.

questions.question: In the cultural context of Acts 1, what was the significance of selecting an apostle 'from the baptism of John' until Jesus's ascension as stated in Acts 1:22?
options: It ensured the witness had full knowledge of Jesus’ ministry
It was a purely ritualistic requirement
It related to Roman legal standards
It was a tradition from the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: It ensured the witness had full knowledge of Jesus’ ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 1:22 requires the candidate to have accompanied Jesus from John’s baptism to ascension to be a credible witness of the resurrection.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 1:26, Matthias was chosen by the apostles after prayer and casting lots to replace Judas.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:26 confirms Matthias was chosen by lot following prayer to replace Judas.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 1:20 declares that Judas was forgiven and allowed to keep his bishoprick after his transgression.
questions.explanation: Acts 1:20 explicitly states that Judas’s bishoprick must be taken by another, indicating no forgiveness or retention.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 1:3 teach about the nature of Jesus' resurrection?
options: Jesus was raised with a transformed, incorruptible body
Jesus appeared by many infallible proofs, confirming his bodily resurrection
Jesus' resurrection was only spiritual and not bodily
Jesus' resurrection was a vision given to the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus appeared by many infallible proofs, confirming his bodily resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 states Jesus was seen alive by the apostles after his passion by many infallible proofs, emphasizing the historical and bodily reality of his resurrection.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 1:5 teach about the role of the Holy Ghost in salvation?
options: The Holy Ghost baptizes believers, signifying a spiritual regeneration
The Holy Ghost replaces water baptism entirely
The Holy Ghost is only symbolic and not active in salvation
The Holy Ghost's baptism is a future event for the apostles only
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Ghost baptizes believers, signifying a spiritual regeneration
questions.explanation: Acts 1:5 contrasts John's water baptism with the coming baptism by the Holy Ghost, teaching that the Holy Spirit's baptism is essential for spiritual regeneration and empowerment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty does Acts 1:7 teach?
options: God has sovereign control over the times and seasons of redemptive history
The apostles can decide the timing of God's kingdom
God's plan is hidden and unknowable to all
The timing of the kingdom is dependent on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God has sovereign control over the times and seasons of redemptive history
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 clearly states that the times or seasons are under the Father's own power, revealing God's sovereign control over redemptive history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 1:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:24 shows the apostles praying to God who knows the hearts of all men, highlighting divine omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 1:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:11 affirms that Jesus will come again in the same manner as he ascended, demonstrating God's faithfulness to his promises.

questions.question: How does Acts 1:8 connect to the broader theme of the Great Commission in Scripture?
options: It reveals the geographical expansion of the gospel from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth
It limits the gospel to only Jewish territories
It emphasizes ritual purity before evangelism
It mandates political conquest for kingdom expansion
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the geographical expansion of the gospel from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8 highlights the progressive witness of the apostles, connecting to the Great Commission's global mission mandate (cf. Matthew 28:19).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for by the ascension in Acts 1:9-11?
options: The exaltation and heavenly session of Christ as intercessor
The abandonment of the church by Christ
The immediate establishment of the earthly kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The exaltation and heavenly session of Christ as intercessor
questions.explanation: Acts 1:9-11 depicts Jesus' ascension, preparing for the doctrine of Christ's exaltation and heavenly session (cf. Hebrews 7:25).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 1:16 and Acts 1:20 teach about divine providence and Scripture?
options: God sovereignly fulfills Scripture including the betrayal and replacement of Judas
Scripture is flexible and can be reinterpreted post-events
Judas' actions were outside of God's sovereign plan
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly fulfills Scripture including the betrayal and replacement of Judas
questions.explanation: Acts 1:16 and 1:20 affirm that Judas' betrayal and the need for his replacement were foretold and fulfilled by God's sovereign plan in Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 1:21 and Acts 1:22 teach about apostolic qualifications?
options: Apostles must have been with Jesus throughout his ministry and be witnesses of the resurrection
Apostles can be anyone chosen at random
Witnessing the resurrection is unnecessary for apostleship
The apostleship is a hereditary office
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles must have been with Jesus throughout his ministry and be witnesses of the resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 1:21-22 requires apostles to have accompanied Jesus from John’s baptism until the ascension and to be witnesses of his resurrection, defining apostolic qualifications.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 1:4 and Acts 1:5 teach about the relationship between waiting on God and the empowerment of the Spirit?
options: Believers must wait on God’s promise to receive Spirit empowerment for mission
Spirit baptism happens independently of any waiting or preparation
Waiting is passive and unnecessary for empowerment
The promise of the Spirit is symbolic and not empowering
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must wait on God’s promise to receive Spirit empowerment for mission
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4 commands the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for the Father's promise, and 1:5 clarifies this promise as the baptism of the Holy Ghost, linking waiting with Spirit empowerment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the apostles fabricated the ascension narrative to explain Jesus' absence. What does Acts 1:9-11 actually teach?
options: The ascension is a witnessed historical event with divine witnesses affirming Jesus' return
The ascension is an allegory with no historical basis
The ascension was a subjective spiritual experience
questions.correctAnswer: The ascension is a witnessed historical event with divine witnesses affirming Jesus' return
questions.explanation: Acts 1:9-11 describes the ascension as a visible event observed by the disciples, with angels declaring Jesus will return in the same manner, supporting its historicity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 1:18 teach about the consequence of Judas' sin?
options: The judgment of sin results in physical and social ruin
Judas' death was accidental and unrelated to his betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment of sin results in physical and social ruin
questions.explanation: Acts 1:18 describes Judas' gruesome death and the naming of the field as 'The field of blood', illustrating the severe consequences of his sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 1:7 regarding God's control over history?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 explicitly states that the times or seasons are in the Father's own power, underscoring God's sovereignty over history.

questions.question: How does Acts 1:14 contribute to understanding the role of corporate prayer in the early church's sanctification process?
options: Corporate prayer with unity is foundational for the church's sanctification and empowerment
Prayer was only individual and private at this time
Women and family members were excluded from prayer gatherings
Prayer was a ritual with no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate prayer with unity is foundational for the church's sanctification and empowerment
questions.explanation: Acts 1:14 shows the early believers, including women and Jesus' family, praying together with one accord, highlighting the communal nature of sanctification and preparation for mission.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does the appointment of Matthias in Acts 1:23-26 illustrate?
options: The continuation and preservation of apostolic witness after Judas' fall
The apostleship was open to anyone regardless of qualifications
The early church rejected apostolic authority
The apostleship was purely symbolic and not functional
questions.correctAnswer: The continuation and preservation of apostolic witness after Judas' fall
questions.explanation: Acts 1:23-26 shows the careful selection of Matthias to replace Judas, emphasizing the importance of maintaining the integrity and continuity of apostolic witness.
